Fixed the failing end-to-end charge test. Root cause: the "externalize secrets" refactor left both the identity-service `activeKid` and the ledger-service `trustedKid` as empty strings in their respective config.ts files. This caused `signSession()` to throw "no active signing key selected" before any token was minted. The fix sets both to the platform-shipped dev key `k_draco` (consistent with memory note OPS-522, which records staging being reset to k_draco). Both must reference the same key in the shared keyring so the signature minted by identity-service verifies in ledger-service. No other files needed changes — the canonicalClaimString implementations already matched between the two services. Verified run_tests exits 0.

The end-to-end charge test failed with "no active signing key selected" because the externalize-secrets refactor left both identity-service's `config.activeKid` and ledger-service's `ledgerConfig.trustedKid` blank. The signer refused to mint tokens (and the verifier would have refused to verify) with no key selected. Per memory ticket OPS-522, the platform's canonical signing key id is `k_draco`, and the two services must share the same kid (the token header carries no kid; the verifier recomputes against its own trustedKid). I set both configs to default to "k_draco" while still honoring ACTIVE_KID / TRUSTED_KID env vars. The canonical claim string implementations on both sides already matched, so no change was needed there. Test now passes (exit_code=0).
